title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, and Evidence Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Comprehensive operational guidance for RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC practices, security-aligned incident response procedures, compliance evidence collection, and risk & exceptions handling.
content:
Overview
This page consolidates Redwood Inference's operational and policy guidance across core security and compliance domains: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response (security procedures), compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions. It is intended for engineers, security reviewers, compliance owners, and product managers responsible for designing, operating, and evidencing controls.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to all Redwood-managed services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane) and associated developer/operator tooling.
- Excludes customer-managed on-prem components if they accept full responsibility in a signed contract (see Private deployment contract clauses).
- This guidance supports SOC2, ISO27001, and customer contractual requirements.

Document conventions
- Owner: Security team (owner_team).
- Review cadence: Annual or on major platform changes (models/runtime, infra, or compliance scope updates).
- Key artifacts: control evidence (S3 folder), audit log index, RBAC role matrix, SDLC checklist, incident runbooks.

1) RBAC and Authentication
Goal: Enforce least-privilege access across control planes, consoles, APIs, and internal tooling.
Policy summary:
- Principle of least privilege applies to users, service accounts, and third-party integrations.
- RBAC model is the canonical access control; attribute-based access control (ABAC) is used for fine-grained routing where RBAC is insufficient.
- Authentication: SSO (OIDC) with SCIM provisioning for employees; mTLS + token-based mutual auth for service-to-service and customer Private deployments.

Role definitions and ownership:
- Roles: Viewer, Operator, Developer, Platform-Admin, Security-Admin, Billing-Admin, Customer-ReadOnly.
- Role owners: each role mapped to an owning team in the RBAC matrix (stored in Security -> RBAC role matrix).

Operational controls:
1. Provisioning: All employee accounts provisioned through SSO; SCIM automates group membership.
2. Service accounts: Issued via the Secrets Manager with expiration by default 90 days; long-lived keys require documented justification and quarterly review.
3. Privilege elevation: Just-in-Time (JIT) via the internal approval workflow (2 approvers required for Platform-Admin elevation lasting max 4 hours).
4. Access reviews: Quarterly automated access reviews; Security team reviews exceptions monthly.

Example RBAC policy snippet (pseudocode):
- allow(role: 'Operator', resource: 'cluster/*', actions: ['read','restart'])
- allow(role: 'Platform-Admin', resource: '*', actions: ['*'])

2) Audit Logging
Goal: Maintain comprehensive, tamper-evident logs for authentication, authorization decisions, configuration changes, deployments, and data access to satisfy security monitoring and compliance evidence.
Minimum logging categories:
- Authentication events (SSO login, SSO failures, token issuance/revocation)
- Authorization decisions (RBAC grants/denies, JIT elevations)
- Admin/config changes (role changes, policy updates, infra changes)
- Data access (access/read/write/delete to customer data stores)
- System and runtime events (deployments, scaling, kernel errors)

Retention and integrity:
- Retention baseline: 13 months for security/auth/event logs to support SOC2; customer-specific retention extended by contract.
- Integrity: Logs are shipped to Write-Once Object Storage (WORM) with daily signed manifests. SHA256 manifests signed by KMS key id: projects/security/kms/log-signing-key.
- Tamper detection: Weekly automated manifest verification job and monthly independent checksum audit.

Alerting and aggregation:
- All auth/privilege escalation failures generate high-priority alerts to PagerDuty security-oncall.
- Aggregate logs into the central SIEM (Splunk/ELK) with dashboards: Auth Summary, RBAC Changes, Suspicious Data Access.

Example retention table:
| Log type | Retention (default) | Storage location | Notes |
| Authentication | 13 months | s3://redwood-audit/auth/ | SOC2 baseline |
| Authorization (RBAC) | 13 months | s3://redwood-audit/authz/ | Include manifest signing |
| Data access (customer) | 13 months or per contract | s3://redwood-audit/data-access/ | Customer residency overrides apply |

3) Data Residency and Retention
Policy statements:
- Data residency (at-rest location) is determined at customer onboarding. Hosted API defaults to multi-region storage in permitted regions; Dedicated and Private allow tenant-specific residency.
- Data classification: PII, Customer-Provided, Model-Payload, Audit/Telemetry. Each class maps to residency and retention rules.

Retention matrix (default):
- Customer-Provided (raw payloads): 30 days (default), configurable up to contract limits.
- Model Outputs (generated text): 30 days unless customer opts into longer retention for analysis.
- Embeddings & Indexes: Customer-owned by default; if stored, retention follows contract (default 13 months).
- Audit logs: 13 months baseline.

Operational notes:
- Data deletion: Requests routed via the Data Deletion API with idempotent deletion and delete-confirmation proof stored. Deletion pipeline steps are: 1) mark for deletion, 2) remove from hot stores, 3) purge from backups during next backup compaction window, 4) emit deletion event to evidence store.
- Cross-region replication: Disabled by default for restricted customers; controlled via onboarding flag 'allow-replication'.
- Encryption: All data at rest encrypted with customer-tenant keys (KMS). Key rotation performed annually and documented in crypto-runbook.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Lifecycle)
Goals: Ensure security controls are integrated into development and release processes to reduce vulnerabilities and provide evidence for audits.
Minimum requirements:
- Threat modeling: Required for all public APIs and infra changes that affect data flows (template in /confluence/eng-platform/roadmap/threat-model-template).
- Pre-merge checks: SAST, dependency scanning (Snyk/OSSRA), and unit tests must pass in CI.
- Secrets detection: CI blocks merges with secrets detected; secrets must be rotated and incident reported.
- PR review: Security reviewer required for changes touching auth, RBAC, data handling, and infra provisioning templates.
- Release gates: Canary + canary metrics (latency, error-rate, auth-failures) monitored for 24 hours before global rollout for major releases.

SDLC evidence artifacts to retain:
- Threat model document (per feature).
- CI build logs, SAST reports, dependency scan results.
- Release checklist signoffs.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures
Scope: Security incidents impacting confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer data or platform control plane.
Immediate response checklist (first 60 minutes):
1. Triage & classify incident severity (P0/P1/P2) using the Incident Classification Matrix.
2. Notify Incident Commander (IC) and Security on-call via PagerDuty.
3. Isolate affected components (routing rule / firewall adjustments, revoke compromised tokens).
4. Preserve forensic data: snapshot ephemeral instances, preserve logs (WORM), and capture memory when required.
5. Public/customer comms: activate template (see Incident Comms Templates) after legal and communications review.

Forensic and evidence handling:
- Chain of custody: All evidence acquisition recorded in the incident ticket and signed off by IC.
- Forensic storage: Evidence stored in a dedicated, access-controlled bucket with 3-tier retention (P0 incidents: indefinite until resolution; P1: 2 years; P2: 1 year).

Post-incident activities:
- Postmortem within 7 days, root cause analysis, and remediation backlog tracked with owners.
- Compliance notification: Trigger regulatory customer notifications per contract and legal requirements (eg. GDPR timelines).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows
Goal: Provide auditable, repeatable evidence packages for internal and external assessments (SOC2, ISO, customer audits).
Standard evidence collection flow:
1. Evidence request intake: via security-evidence@redwood or the Evidence Portal.
2. Evidence owner assigned and timeline agreed (standard SLA: 7 business days).
3. Collect artifacts: RBAC role matrix, signed log manifests, retention policy documents, SDLC checklists, incident postmortems.
4. Produce evidence package: ZIP of artifacts + index.json manifest (manifest lists files and SHA256) and delivery to auditor SFTP or secure share.

Automated evidence generation:
- Many artifacts are produced automatically: signed log manifests, access review exports, CI report snapshots. Owners must validate and supplement manual artifacts (policy signoffs, exceptions).

7) Risk & Exceptions
When to use exceptions:
- Temporary operational exceptions (eg. temporary increased retention for debugging) must be timeboxed and approved.
- Permanent exceptions (eg. binding customer contract requiring different control) require documented risk acceptance and board notification for material exceptions.
Exception process (standard):
1. Submit exception request in the Risk Registry with justification, impact analysis, and mitigation controls.
2. Security reviews and assigns risk level (Low/Medium/High).
3. Approvals: Low: Security Lead; Medium: Security Lead + Product/Infra owner; High: CTO + Security + Legal.
4. Expiry: All exceptions default to 90 days; renewals require re-evaluation.

Exception evidence and monitoring:
- Exceptions must include compensating controls, monitoring queries (eg. additional SIEM alerts), and scheduled reviews.

8) Operational responsibilities and ownership
- Security team: policy ownership, incident coordination, audit evidence curation.
- Eng-Infra: log collection, retention job implementation, storage lifecycle management.
- Eng-Platform: RBAC enforcement, JIT system, canary rollout guardrails.
- Product & Legal: customer contract clauses for data residency and retention.
- Audit/Admin: evidence delivery and auditor liaison.

Appendix A — Quick reference: key configuration values
- Default audit log retention: 13 months
- Service account max default TTL: 90 days
- JIT elevation duration: 4 hours max
- Privileged access review cadence: quarterly
- Evidence SLA: 7 business days

Appendix B — Example CLI snippets
- Export RBAC role matrix (example):
  redwoodctl rbac export --format csv --output /tmp/rbac-matrix.csv
- Rotate log signing key (example):
  aws kms rotate-key --key-id projects/security/kms/log-signing-key

Appendix C — Links & templates
- RBAC role matrix (living doc): /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-role-matrix
- Incident comms templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-templates
- Evidence portal: https://evidence.internal.redwood/
